replies.author: veetance
replies.body:
The only thing off here is your confirmation bias.  If this same dev log came out in 2003 people would be amazed...

It's because of game engines and AI that people now take things for granted. Even if no AI was used people will still hate.

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body: It’s not 2003. AI and game engines have made it easier to game dev so it’s natural to expect people to do better.

replies.author: veetance
replies.body: It's natural to not be rude while giving feedback, and have actual critical feedback instead of just saying "something is off" regurgitating Ai hate... Maybe you could have given constructive feedback...The creator literally told you, no shadows yet and so on... You could have defined what "better" means in a way that shows authority and perhaps, I'd know you're not just a piece of ....

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body:
I literally said something was off and that I couldn’t put my finger on exactly what. 

Is being uncertain about something “rude” now? Grow a thicker skin.

replies.author: veetance
replies.body:
How can you dismissing someone's efforts with low level critiques such as "something is off, you can't put your finger on it"

If you knew what you were talking about you would have helped the creator advance by giving actual constructive feedback and how they could make it "better " what they did right and how they can improve.

You are the kind of person on a team project that will just say, "something is off guys fix it"

My skin is venta black 🖤, but I don't appreciate weak indirect dismissive comments intended to demoralize human effort, if you actually gave feedback that advanced the artist you'd be making a reasonable point besides the obvious, naive and senseless doom filled AI hate.

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body:
It’s not my job to give feedback. I’m not your project manager. 

As a regular old member of the public I can say “somethings off” without being specific. 

I’m honoured you value my opinion so much but sorry. “Something is off” is all I have to give.

replies.author: PlaidWorld
replies.body: It’s the lighting system being used.

replies.author: Aaroncxc
replies.body: What would you change ? Today i added a post processing tool because i also think the light and shadow situation could be much better.

replies.author: PlaidWorld
replies.body: Cube maps for lighting across all object might help. They can remove the kind of gray / sterile look you see in older game engines. That might be 1 easy thing to try. You really just need 1 environmental cube map thats applied to every thing. It basically fakes global illumination type solutions.

comments.author: AgenticGameDev
comments.body:
The art is not coherent. Great effort but it feels like every art asset is following different rules. Resolution and design differ. As AI to describe each art style for the seperate objects one chat per object and I guess it will give you good guidance on what is different. Then decide what is your games art style. 

Also no game feel stuff. But I guess that will come later maybe but that feels of. It should feel fun to harvest and plant as that is core.

Keep it up:)

replies.author: Aaroncxc
replies.body: I think you completely right ! I will try to work out a stronger art guide and will try to create a clearer art language! But do you think it has also something to do with the post processing wich feels off ? The light and shadows ? I’m not sure…

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: Hard to tell before you nail the art guidelines. It could work like that with right art guidelines or you could be 100% right. Based on your comment I guess your vision is in that area. So go for it once you look in.
